local_kernel: For fixed unit x, x^e=x^e' mod n iff ord_n(x) divides e-e'; kernel=ord_n(x)Z.
finite_sample_kernel: For S={x_i}, simultaneous equality iff lcm_i ord_n(x_i) divides e-e'; this lcm is exp(<S>).

single_collision.setup: Delta=2^s u, u odd, r_p=ord_p(x)=2^a m_p, r_q=ord_q(x)=2^b m_q
single_collision.chain: z_j=x^(u*2^j); z_j=1 mod p iff j>=a, and mod q iff j>=b
single_collision.success_criterion: factor extraction by first pre-1 state succeeds iff a != b
single_collision.failure_locus: a=b; if a=b>0 the first pre-1 state is -1 modulo both primes, while a=b=0 starts at 1
single_collision.extractor_hidden_inputs: NONE: only n,x,Delta; proof-side p,q/orders are ground truth only

random_unit_probability.depth_distribution: Pr[a=0]=2^-A; Pr[a=t]=2^(t-1-A) for 1<=t<=A, independently at q

global_collision.criterion: Two exponent maps agree on every unit iff e-e' is a multiple of lambda(n)=lcm(p-1,q-1).
global_collision.consequence: One exposed nonzero global difference is an annihilating exponent; random-unit collapse factors with the exact single-unit probability and at least 1/2 per independent base.
global_collision.classification: This is the classical multiple-of-group-exponent/order-to-factor reduction, not a collision-generation algorithm.

multiple_certificates.safe_aggregation: L=lcm_i Delta_i annihilates H=<x_i>; gcd_i Delta_i has no universal annihilator guarantee.
multiple_certificates.full_subgroup_barrier: All H-combinations fail iff the 2-primary H_2 is the graph of an isomorphism between cyclic local projection subgroups of equal order.
multiple_certificates.strict_gain_condition: For k>=2 and min(A,B)>=2 aggregation can be strictly stronger than running each certificate separately.
multiple_certificates.strict_witness: n=65, x1=57, x2=47, Delta1=Delta2=4: both singles fail; x1*x2=14 and L=4 yields gcd(14-1,65)=13.

barrier_scope: The equal-depth/diagonal-graph statements are exact barriers for the collision-driven 2-adic CRT-square-root mechanism. They are not an information-theoretic claim that n cannot be factored by some unrelated method.
